response.sql:
WITH qualifying AS (
  SELECT ID
  FROM Laboratory
  GROUP BY ID
  HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN `U-PRO` = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
     AND SUM(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
),
per_patient AS (
  SELECT l.ID,
         AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt,
         AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_tat_diff
  FROM Laboratory l
  JOIN qualifying q ON q.ID = l.ID
  GROUP BY l.ID
)
SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_pt_averages,
       AVG(avg_tat_diff) AS avg_of_tat_diff_averages
FROM per_patient;

assumptions.assumption: '-' is compared as an exact string match against the stored TEXT values, with no trimming or case handling. The qualifying U-PRO and RA records may be different records of the same patient.

TAT minus TAT2 is computed per laboratory record and then averaged, so any record with a NULL in TAT or TAT2 is skipped for that average. Missing PT values are skipped by AVG. A patient with no non-null PT or TAT-TAT2 value contributes NULL and is dropped from the outer average.

alternatives.interpretation: Take the difference of the per-patient averages, AVG(TAT) minus AVG(TAT2), rather than the average of the per-record differences. Each average then uses its own non-null records.
